cards.text: This is a psalm of Asaph, chief of the Levite musicians David put before the ark of the LORD (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). And it opens LOUD. The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth.

cards.question: God summons the earth "from where the sun rises to where it sets." Who is God calling?

answers.text: The whole earth east to west

cards.text: I holler across my bakery and barely reach the cooling racks, and God just summoned the WHOLE EARTH. From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says that as God approaches, He comes quietly.

cards.text: Consuming fire goes before Him, and a tempest rages around Him. And I used to brag about how hot MY oven runs.
Then God summons the heavens above and the earth. Heaven AND earth, called in at once. That is not a casual meeting, friend.

cards.question: God summons the heavens above and the earth. What does He call them in for?

answers.text: So He may judge His people
So they can praise His name
So He can make them new

cards.text: Then comes the call to gather God's saints. These are His people, joined to Him by a covenant.

cards.question: God's saints made a covenant with Him by ___
Asaph says the heavens proclaim God's righteousness, for God Himself is ___

cards.text: After a Selah, God Himself speaks: "Hear, O My people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God." Testify AGAINST you. Oof.

cards.question: True or false: God tells His people He is rebuking them for their sacrifices.

cards.text: Nope, their burnt offerings are ever before Him. But He has no need for a bull from their stall or goats from their pens.

cards.question: Why doesn't God need a bull or goats from His people?

answers.text: Every beast of the forest is His

cards.text: The cattle on a thousand hills, every bird in the mountains, the creatures of the field. ALL His. Me? I've got ONE cookie planet, and the bakery takes up the WHOLE thing.

cards.question: True or false: God says that if He were hungry, He would tell His people.

cards.text: He wouldn't, because the world is His, and the fullness thereof. Then He asks, "Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?"

cards.question: What offering does God tell His people to sacrifice to Him?

cards.text: He also tells them to fulfill their vows to the Most High. Then He makes them a promise for the hard days.

cards.question: "Call upon Me in the day of trouble," God says. Then He will ___ you, and you will ___ Him.

cards.text: Then God turns to the wicked: "What right have you to recite My statutes and to bear My covenant on your lips?"

cards.question: The wicked can recite God's statutes just fine. So what's God's problem with them?

answers.text: They add rules of their own
They recite them only in private

cards.text: They cast His words behind them, tossed over the shoulder like a receipt nobody's ever gonna need. Trust me, I spent YEARS in a drawer next to those.

cards.question: True or false: God says that when the wicked see a thief, they keep their distance.

cards.text: They throw in their lot with adulterers too. Evil? Unleashed. Deceit? Harnessed. That mouth is clocking OVERTIME.

cards.question: God says the wicked sit and slander someone. Who?

cards.text: They did all of this, and God kept silent. Now watch what they made of that.

cards.question: God stayed silent while the wicked did all this. What did they think that meant?

answers.text: That God was just like them

cards.question: True or false: God tells the wicked He will go on keeping silent.

cards.text: Now He rebukes them and accuses them to their face. The silence is OVER.
Then God warns the ones who forget Him: "Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you:"

cards.question: God's last words are about the thank offering. The one who sacrifices a thank offering ___ God.
And to the one who rightly orders his way, God will show the ___ of God.

findings.problem: The opening card says the psalm "opens LOUD." That answers card 4 before it's asked: card 4 asks whether God comes quietly as He approaches (Psalm 50:3). Psalm 50:1 also says only that God speaks. It never says He speaks loudly.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says God "summons the earth." The question then quotes "from where the sun rises to where it sets" and asks who God is calling. Both together hand the baker the answer "The whole earth east to west."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "Then God summons the heavens above and the earth. Heaven AND earth, called in at once. That is not a casual meeting, friend."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "So they can praise His name" is close to Psalm 50:6, where the heavens proclaim His righteousness. A baker could argue that the heavens are called to praise Him.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the Selah line with the quote of Psalm 50:7, then "Testify AGAINST you." and then "Oof."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: "The cattle on a thousand hills... ALL His. Me? I've got ONE cookie planet..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The second blank ("you will ___ Him") asks the baker to guess the exact word "honor" in Psalm 50:15. Nothing earlier makes "honor" a better pick than "follow," so the baker can only guess the wording of the line.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: "They throw in their lot with adulterers too. Evil? Unleashed. Deceit? Harnessed. That mouth is clocking OVERTIME."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the last words of Psalm 50:23 ("salvation" against "glory" or "wisdom"). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out "salvation" over "glory."

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
